scenes.text: When your group asks about the real world, Vibe goes to the live web with TinyFish.
Ask about Saturday's weather, and Vibe runs a TinyFish search, then fetches the forecast pages as clean markdown, fresh every single time.
Every fact comes back with its source and the moment it was retrieved, so anyone in the chat can check it.
Follow-up questions work the same way: park hours, entry fees, straight from the official pages.

Vibe can only fetch pages its search actually found, so it can't invent a source. Each reply gets a tight budget of two searches and three fetches, so answers stay fast. And the TinyFish key never leaves our servers.
Live web research, right inside your group chat. Vibe, powered by TinyFish.
Vibe remembers people, and Supermemory is how.
Maya mentions she's vegetarian in the class chat. Nobody tags Vibe. A few minutes after the chat goes quiet, Vibe quietly learns it in the background.
Supermemory gives every party its own space, and every person two more: private, and approved. A new fact always starts private.
Nothing is shared until Maya approves it, and switches it on for a specific party.

When someone asks Vibe, it searches the party's history and each opted-in member's approved facts, putting schedules, diets and accessibility first. So the Sedona plan already knows Maya is vegetarian.

Say it twice, and Supermemory merges it into one fact. Change it to vegan, and the very next answer follows. Every result is double-checked against DynamoDB, so a deleted fact can never sneak back in.
Memory with consent. Vibe, powered by Supermemory.
Vibe runs entirely on AWS, built to be fast, reliable and secure from day one.
CloudFront and S3 serve the app on our own domain, and Amazon Cognito handles sign-in.
Every message goes through API Gateway to Lambda, and lands in DynamoDB in a single transaction, together with an outbox record, so no work is ever lost.
DynamoDB Streams wake a dispatcher, which queues AI work in SQS FIFO queues, keeping every party's work in order.
Lambda workers call Claude Haiku 4.5 on Amazon Bedrock. It powers the replies, the memory extraction, and even picks each party's theme.
AppSync Events pushes every update live to everyone in the party, and Amazon SES delivers the email invites.
EventBridge sweeps up stuck work every five minutes, secrets stay encrypted in Parameter Store with least-privilege IAM, CloudWatch keeps the logs, and the whole stack is defined in CDK.
Serverless, event-driven, and ready to scale. Vibe, built on AWS.
